controls.statement: IP phones used in public areas do not have the ability to access data networks, voicemail and directory services.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Internet Protocol phones in public areas

controls.statement: Microphones (including headsets and USB handsets) and webcams are not used with non-SECRET workstations in SECRET areas.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Microphones and webcams

controls.statement: Microphones (including headsets and USB handsets) and webcams are not used with non-TOP SECRET workstations in TOP SECRET areas.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Microphones and webcams

controls.statement: A denial of service response plan for video conferencing and IP telephony services is developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Denial of service response plan

controls.statement:
A denial of service response plan for video conferencing and IP telephony services contains the following:

- how to identify signs of a denial-of-service attack
- how to identify the source of a denial-of-service attack
- how capabilities can be maintained during a denial-of-service attack
- what actions can be taken to respond to a denial-of-service attack.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony / Denial of service response plan

controls.statement: An MFD usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Multifunction device usage policy

controls.statement: MFDs are not connected to digital telephone systems.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Connecting multifunction devices to digital telephone systems

controls.statement: Users authenticate to MFDs before they can print, scan or copy documents.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Authenticating to multifunction devices

controls.statement: Authentication measures for MFDs are the same strength as those used for workstations on networks they are connected to.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Authenticating to multifunction devices

controls.statement: MFDs are not used to scan or copy documents above the sensitivity or classification of networks they are connected to.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Scanning and copying documents on multifunction devices

controls.statement: Use of MFDs for printing, scanning and copying purposes, including the capture of shadow copies of documents, are centrally logged.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Logging multifunction device use

controls.statement: MFDs are placed in areas where their use can be observed.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Multifunction devices / Observing multifunction device use

controls.statement: Fax machines, and online fax services, are not used for sending or receiving fax messages.
controls.topic: Guidelines for communications systems / Fax machines and services / Sending and receiving fax messages

controls.statement: Legal advice is sought prior to allowing privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers to access systems or data.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers

controls.statement: Personnel using privately owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data have enforced separation of classified data and personal data.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers

controls.statement: Personnel using privately owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data are prevented from storing classified data on their privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers

controls.statement: Personnel using privately owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data are disallowed from granting access to unapproved artificial intelligence agents.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers

controls.statement: Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers do not access SECRET and TOP SECRET systems or data.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers

controls.statement: Personnel using organisation-owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access classified systems or data have enforced separation of classified data and personal data.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Organisation-owned mobile devices and desktop computers

controls.statement: Mobile devices and desktop computers access the internet via an organisation’s internet gateway rather than via a direct connection to the internet.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Mobile devices and desktop computers accessing the internet

controls.statement: When accessing an organisation’s network via a VPN connection, split tunnelling is disabled.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Enterprise mobility / Mobile devices and desktop computers accessing the internet

controls.statement: A mobile device management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Mobile device management policy

controls.statement: Mobile Device Management solutions that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against the Protection Profile for Mobile Device Management, version 4.0 or later, are used to enforce mobile device management policy.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Mobile device management policy

controls.statement: Mobile devices that access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data use mobile platforms that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against the Protection Profile for Mobile Device Fundamentals, version 3.3 or later, and are operated in accordance with the latest version of their associated ASD security configuration guide.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Approved mobile platforms

controls.statement: Mobile devices that access SECRET or TOP SECRET systems or data use mobile platforms that have been issued an Approval for Use by ASD and are operated in accordance with the latest version of their associated Australian Communications Security Instruction.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Approved mobile platforms

controls.statement: Mobile devices encrypt their internal storage and any removable media using ASD-approved cryptography.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Encrypted storage

controls.statement: SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices do not use removable media unless approved beforehand by ASD.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Encrypted storage

controls.statement: Mobile devices encrypt all sensitive or classified data communicated over public network infrastructure using ASD-approved cryptography.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Encrypted communications

controls.statement: Mobile applications encrypt all sensitive or classified data communicated over public network infrastructure using ASD-approved cryptography.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Encrypted communications

controls.statement: Mobile devices are configured to operate in a supervised (or equivalent) mode.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security

controls.statement: Mobile devices are configured to enforce separation between organisational and personal mobile applications and data.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security

controls.statement: Mobile devices are configured with always on VPN functionality.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security

controls.statement: Mobile devices are configured with remote locate and wipe functionality.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security

controls.statement: Mobile devices are configured with secure password-based lock screens.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security

controls.statement: Mobile devices are configured to prevent data transfers over Universal Serial Bus connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security

controls.statement: Mobile devices prevent personnel from installing non-approved applications once provisioned.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security

controls.statement: Mobile devices prevent personnel from disabling or modifying security functionality once provisioned.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security

controls.statement: Security updates are applied to mobile devices as soon as they become available.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device management / Maintaining mobile device security

controls.statement: A mobile device usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Mobile device usage policy

controls.statement: Personnel are advised of the sensitivity or classification permitted for voice and data communications when using mobile devices.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Personnel awareness

controls.statement:
Personnel are advised to take the following precautions when using mobile devices:

- never leave mobile devices or removable media unattended, including by placing them in checked-in luggage or leaving them in hotel safes
- never store credentials with mobile devices that they grant access to, such as in laptop computer bags
- never lend mobile devices or removable media to untrusted people, even if briefly
- never allow untrusted people to connect their mobile devices or removable media to your mobile devices, including for charging
- never connect mobile devices to designated charging stations or wall outlet charging ports
- never use gifted or unauthorised peripherals, chargers or removable media with mobile devices
- never use removable media for data transfers or backups that have not been checked for malicious code beforehand
- avoid reuse of removable media once used with other parties’ systems or mobile devices
- avoid connecting mobile devices to open or untrusted Wi-Fi networks
- consider disabling any communications capabilities of mobile devices when not in use, such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Near Field Communication and ultra-wideband
- consider periodically rebooting mobile devices
- consider using a VPN connection to encrypt all cellular and wireless communications
- consider using encrypted email or messaging apps for all communications.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Personnel awareness

controls.statement: Paging, Multimedia Message Service, Short Message Service and messaging apps are not used to communicate sensitive or classified data.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using paging, message services and messaging apps

controls.statement: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices are configured to remain undiscoverable to other Bluetooth devices except during Bluetooth pairing.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using Bluetooth functionality

controls.statement: Bluetooth pairing for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices is performed using Secure Connections, preferably with Numeric Comparison if supported.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using Bluetooth functionality

controls.statement: Bluetooth pairing for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices is performed in a manner such that connections are only made between intended Bluetooth devices.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using Bluetooth functionality

controls.statement: Bluetooth pairings for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices are removed when there is no longer a requirement for their use.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using Bluetooth functionality

controls.statement: Bluetooth functionality is not enabled on SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using Bluetooth functionality

controls.statement: Mobile devices are not connected to the infotainment systems of connected vehicles.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Connecting mobile devices to connected vehicles

controls.statement: Sensitive or classified data is not viewed on mobile devices within or near connected vehicles.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using mobile devices within or near connected vehicles

controls.statement: Sensitive or classified phone calls and conversations are not conducted within or near connected vehicles.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using mobile devices within or near connected vehicles

controls.statement: Sensitive or classified data is not viewed on mobile devices in public locations unless care is taken to reduce the chance of the screen of a mobile device being observed.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using mobile devices in public spaces

controls.statement: Privacy filters are applied to the screens of SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using mobile devices in public spaces

controls.statement: Sensitive or classified phone calls and conversations are not conducted in public locations unless care is taken to reduce the chance of conversations being overheard.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Using mobile devices in public spaces

controls.statement: Mobile devices are kept under continual direct supervision when being actively used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Maintaining control of mobile devices

controls.statement: Mobile devices are carried or stored in a secured state when not being actively used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Maintaining control of mobile devices

controls.statement: If unable to carry or store mobile devices in a secured state, they are physically transferred in a security briefcase or an approved multi-use satchel, pouch or transit bag.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Maintaining control of mobile devices

controls.statement: Mobile device emergency sanitisation processes, and supporting mobile device emergency sanitisation procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Mobile device emergency sanitisation processes and procedures

controls.statement: If a cryptographic zeroise or sanitise function is provided for cryptographic keys on a SECRET or TOP SECRET mobile device, the function is used as part of mobile device emergency sanitisation processes and procedures.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Mobile device emergency sanitisation processes and procedures

controls.statement: Personnel are advised of privacy and security risks when travelling overseas with mobile devices.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Before travelling overseas with mobile devices

controls.statement:
If travelling overseas with mobile devices to high or extreme risk countries, personnel are:

- issued with newly provisioned user accounts, mobile devices and removable media from a pool of dedicated travel devices which are used solely for work-related activities
- advised on how to apply and inspect tamper seals to key areas of mobile devices
- advised to avoid taking any personal mobile devices, especially if rooted or jailbroken.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Before travelling overseas with mobile devices

controls.statement:
Before travelling overseas with mobile devices, personnel take the following actions:

- record all details of the mobile devices being taken, such as product types, serial numbers and International Mobile Equipment Identity numbers
- update all operating systems and applications
- remove all non-essential data, applications and user accounts
- backup all remaining data, applications and settings.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / Before travelling overseas with mobile devices

controls.statement:
Personnel report the potential compromise of mobile devices, removable media or credentials to their organisation as soon as possible, especially if they:

- provide credentials to foreign government officials
- decrypt mobile devices for foreign government officials
- have mobile devices taken out of sight by foreign government officials
- have mobile devices or removable media stolen, including if later returned
- lose mobile devices or removable media, including if later found
- observe unusual behaviour of mobile devices.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / While travelling overseas with mobile devices

controls.statement:
Upon returning from travelling overseas with mobile devices, personnel take the following actions:

- sanitise and reset mobile devices, including all removable media
- decommission any credentials that left their possession during their travel
- report if significant doubt exists as to the integrity of any mobile devices or removable media.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / After travelling overseas with mobile devices

controls.statement:
If returning from travelling overseas with mobile devices to high or extreme risk countries, personnel take the following additional actions:

- reset credentials used with mobile devices, including those used for remote access to their organisation’s systems
- monitor user accounts for any indicators of compromise, such as failed logon attempts.
controls.topic: Guidelines for enterprise mobility / Mobile device usage / After travelling overseas with mobile devices

controls.statement: If procuring an evaluated product, a product that has completed a PP-based evaluation, including against all applicable PP modules (as well as a software bill of materials assessment if applicable), is selected in preference to one that has completed an EAL-based evaluation.
controls.topic: Guidelines for evaluated products / Evaluated product procurement / Evaluated product selection

controls.statement: Evaluated products are delivered in a manner consistent with any delivery procedures defined in associated evaluation documentation.
controls.topic: Guidelines for evaluated products / Evaluated product procurement / Delivery of evaluated products

controls.statement: When procuring high assurance information technology (IT) equipment, ASD is contacted for any equipment-specific delivery procedures.
controls.topic: Guidelines for evaluated products / Evaluated product procurement / Delivery of evaluated products

controls.statement: Evaluated products are installed, configured, administered and operated in an evaluated configuration and in accordance with vendor guidance.
controls.topic: Guidelines for evaluated products / Evaluated product usage / Using evaluated products

controls.statement: High assurance IT equipment is installed, configured, administered and operated in an evaluated configuration and in accordance with ASD guidance.
controls.topic: Guidelines for evaluated products / Evaluated product usage / Using evaluated products

controls.statement: An IT equipment management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / IT equipment management policy

controls.statement: Approved configurations for IT equipment are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Hardening IT equipment configurations

controls.statement: IT equipment is hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Hardening IT equipment configurations

controls.statement: A networked IT equipment register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / IT equipment registers

controls.statement: A non-networked IT equipment register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / IT equipment registers

controls.statement: IT equipment, except for high assurance IT equipment, is labelled with protective markings reflecting its sensitivity or classification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Labelling IT equipment

controls.statement: ASD’s approval is sought before applying labels to external surfaces of high assurance IT equipment.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Labelling high assurance IT equipment

controls.statement: IT equipment is classified based on the highest sensitivity or classification of data that it is approved for processing, storing or communicating.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Classifying IT equipment

controls.statement: IT equipment is handled in a manner suitable for its sensitivity or classification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment usage / Handling IT equipment

controls.statement: ASD’s approval is sought before undertaking any maintenance or repairs to high assurance IT equipment.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / Maintenance or repairs of high assurance IT equipment

controls.statement: Maintenance or repairs of IT equipment are carried out on site by an appropriately cleared technician.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / On-site maintenance or repairs

controls.statement: If an appropriately cleared technician is not used to undertake maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, the IT equipment and associated media are sanitised before maintenance or repairs.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / On-site maintenance or repairs

controls.statement:
If an appropriately cleared technician is not used to undertake maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, the technician is escorted by someone who:

- has the authority to direct the technician
- is appropriately cleared and briefed
- is sufficiently familiar with the IT equipment to understand the work being undertaken
- takes all responsible measures to ensure the integrity of the IT equipment
- takes due care to ensure that data is not disclosed.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / On-site maintenance or repairs

controls.statement: IT equipment maintained or repaired off site is handled at facilities approved for handling the sensitivity or classification of the IT equipment.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / Off-site maintenance or repairs

controls.statement: Following maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, it is inspected to confirm that it retains its approved configuration and that no unauthorised modifications have been made.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment maintenance or repairs / Inspection of IT equipment following maintenance or repairs

controls.statement: IT equipment sanitisation processes, and supporting IT equipment sanitisation procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / IT equipment sanitisation processes and procedures

controls.statement: IT equipment destruction processes, and supporting IT equipment destruction procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / IT equipment destruction processes and procedures

controls.statement: IT equipment containing media is sanitised by removing the media from the IT equipment or by sanitising the media in situ.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising IT equipment

controls.statement: IT equipment that cannot be sanitised is destroyed.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising IT equipment

controls.statement: IT equipment, including associated media, that is located overseas and has processed, stored or communicated AUSTEO or AGAO data, is sanitised in situ.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising highly sensitive IT equipment

controls.statement: IT equipment, including associated media, that is located overseas and has processed, stored or communicated AUSTEO or AGAO data that cannot be sanitised in situ, is returned to Australia for destruction.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising highly sensitive IT equipment

controls.statement: High assurance IT equipment is destroyed prior to its disposal.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Destroying high assurance IT equipment

controls.statement: At least three pages of random text with no blank areas are printed on each colour printer cartridge or MFD print drum.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices

controls.statement: MFD print drums and image transfer rollers are inspected and destroyed if there is remnant toner that cannot be removed or a print is visible on the image transfer roller.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices

controls.statement: Printer and MFD platens are inspected and destroyed if any text or images are retained on the platen.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices

controls.statement: Printers and MFDs are checked to ensure no pages are trapped in the paper path due to a paper jam.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices

controls.statement: When unable to sanitise printer cartridges or MFD print drums, they are destroyed as per electrostatic memory devices.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices

controls.statement: Printer ribbons in printers and MFDs are removed and destroyed.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising printers and multifunction devices

controls.statement: Televisions and computer monitors with minor burn-in or image persistence are sanitised by displaying a solid white image on the screen for an extended period.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising televisions and computer monitors

controls.statement: Televisions and computer monitors that cannot be sanitised are destroyed.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising televisions and computer monitors

controls.statement:
Memory in network devices is sanitised using the following processes, in order of preference:

- following device-specific guidance provided in evaluation documentation
- following vendor sanitisation guidance
- loading a dummy configuration file, performing a factory reset and then reinstalling firmware.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment sanitisation and destruction / Sanitising network devices

controls.statement: IT equipment disposal processes, and supporting IT equipment disposal procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment disposal / IT equipment disposal processes and procedures

controls.statement: Labels and markings indicating the owner, sensitivity, classification or any other marking that can associate IT equipment with its prior use are removed prior to its disposal.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment disposal / Disposal of IT equipment

controls.statement: When disposing of IT equipment that has been designed or modified to meet emanation security standards, ASD is contacted for requirements relating to its disposal.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment disposal / Disposal of IT equipment

controls.statement: Following sanitisation, destruction or declassification, a formal administrative decision is made to release IT equipment, or its waste, into the public domain.
controls.topic: Guidelines for information technology equipment / IT equipment disposal / Disposal of IT equipment

controls.statement: A media management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Media management policy

controls.statement: A removable media usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Removable media usage policy

controls.statement: A removable media register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Removable media register

controls.statement: Media, except for internally mounted fixed media within information technology equipment, is labelled with protective markings reflecting its sensitivity or classification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Labelling media

controls.statement: Media is classified to the highest sensitivity or classification of data it stores, unless the media has been classified to a higher sensitivity or classification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Classifying media

controls.statement: Media is only used with systems that are authorised to process, store or communicate its sensitivity or classification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Classifying media

controls.statement: Any media connected to a system with a higher sensitivity or classification than the media is reclassified to the higher sensitivity or classification, unless the media is read-only or the system has a mechanism through which read-only access can be ensured.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Reclassifying media

controls.statement: Before reclassifying media to a lower sensitivity or classification, the media is sanitised or destroyed, and a formal administrative decision is made to reclassify it.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Reclassifying media

controls.statement: All data stored on media is encrypted using ASD-approved cryptography.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Encrypting media

controls.statement: Full disk encryption, or partial encryption where access controls only allow writing to encrypted partitions or volumes, is implemented when encrypting media.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Encrypting media

controls.statement: Pre-boot authentication using passwords, or managed network-based key release, is implemented for media containing encrypted system volumes.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Encrypting media

controls.statement: Media is handled in a manner suitable for its sensitivity or classification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Handling media

controls.statement: Media is sanitised before it is used for the first time.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Sanitising media before first use

controls.statement: Media is sanitised before it is reused in a different security domain.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Sanitising media before first use

controls.statement: When transferring data manually between two systems belonging to different security domains, write-once media is used unless the destination system has a mechanism through which read-only access can be ensured.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Using media for data transfers

controls.statement: When transferring data manually between two systems belonging to different security domains, rewritable media is sanitised after each data transfer.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media usage / Using media for data transfers

controls.statement: Media sanitisation processes, and supporting media sanitisation procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Media sanitisation processes and procedures

controls.statement: Volatile media is sanitised by removing its power for at least 10 minutes.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Volatile media sanitisation

controls.statement: SECRET and TOP SECRET volatile media is sanitised by overwriting it at least once in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Volatile media sanitisation

controls.statement: Following sanitisation, TOP SECRET volatile media retains its classification if it stored static data for an extended period, or had data repeatedly stored on or written to the same memory location for an extended period.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Treatment of volatile media following sanitisation

controls.statement: Non-volatile magnetic media is sanitised by overwriting it at least once (or three times if pre-2001 or under 15 GB) in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile magnetic media sanitisation

controls.statement: The host-protected area and device configuration overlay table are reset prior to the sanitisation of non-volatile magnetic hard drives.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile magnetic media sanitisation

controls.statement: The ATA secure erase command is used, in addition to block overwriting software, to ensure the growth defects table of non-volatile magnetic hard drives is overwritten.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile magnetic media sanitisation

controls.statement: Following sanitisation, SECRET and TOP SECRET non-volatile magnetic media retains its classification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Treatment of non-volatile magnetic media following sanitisation

controls.statement: Non-volatile EPROM media is sanitised by applying three times the manufacturer’s specified ultraviolet erasure time and then overwriting it at least once in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile erasable programmable read-only memory media sanitisation

controls.statement: Non-volatile EEPROM media is sanitised by overwriting it at least once in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile electrically erasable programmable read-only memory media sanitisation

controls.statement: Following sanitisation, SECRET and TOP SECRET non-volatile EPROM and EEPROM media retains its classification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Treatment of non-volatile erasable and electrically erasable programmable read-only memory media following sanitisation

controls.statement: Non-volatile flash memory media is sanitised by overwriting it at least twice in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Non-volatile flash memory media sanitisation

controls.statement: Following sanitisation, SECRET and TOP SECRET non-volatile flash memory media retains its classification.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Treatment of non-volatile flash memory media following sanitisation

controls.statement: Media that cannot be successfully sanitised is destroyed prior to its disposal.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media sanitisation / Media that cannot be successfully sanitised

controls.statement: Media destruction processes, and supporting media destruction procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction processes and procedures

controls.statement:
The following media types are destroyed prior to their disposal:

- microfiche and microfilm
- optical discs
- programmable read-only memory
- read-only memory
- other types of media that cannot be sanitised.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media that cannot be sanitised

controls.statement: Security Construction and Equipment Committee-approved equipment or ASIO-approved equipment is used when destroying media.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction equipment

controls.statement: If using degaussers to destroy media, degaussers evaluated by the United States’ National Security Agency are used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction equipment

controls.statement: Equipment that is capable of reducing microform to a fine powder, with resultant particles not showing more than five consecutive characters per particle upon microscopic inspection, is used to destroy microfiche and microfilm.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods

controls.statement: Electrostatic memory devices are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator or grinder/sander.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods

controls.statement: Magnetic floppy disks are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, degausser or by cutting.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods

controls.statement: Magnetic hard disks are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, grinder/sander or degausser.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods

controls.statement: Magnetic tapes are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, degausser or by cutting.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods

controls.statement: Optical disks are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, grinder/sander or by cutting.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods

controls.statement: Semiconductor memory is destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill or disintegrator.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods

controls.statement: Media destroyed using a hammer mill, disintegrator, grinder/sander or by cutting results in media waste particles no larger than 9 mm.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Media destruction methods

controls.statement: The resulting media waste particles from the destruction of SECRET media is stored and handled as OFFICIAL if less than or equal to 3 mm, PROTECTED if greater than 3 mm and less than or equal to 6 mm, or SECRET if greater than 6 mm and less than or equal to 9 mm.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Treatment of media waste particles

controls.statement: The resulting media waste particles from the destruction of TOP SECRET media is stored and handled as OFFICIAL if less than or equal to 3 mm, or SECRET if greater than 3 mm and less than or equal to 9 mm.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Treatment of media waste particles

controls.statement: Magnetic media is destroyed using a degausser with a suitable magnetic field strength and magnetic orientation.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Degaussing magnetic media

controls.statement: Product-specific directions provided by degausser manufacturers are followed.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Degaussing magnetic media

controls.statement: Following the use of a degausser, magnetic media is physically damaged by deforming any internal platters.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Degaussing magnetic media

controls.statement: The destruction of media is performed under the supervision of at least one cleared person.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Supervision of destruction

controls.statement: Personnel supervising the destruction of media supervise its handling to the point of destruction and ensure that the destruction is completed successfully.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Supervision of destruction

controls.statement: The destruction of media storing accountable material is performed under the supervision of at least two cleared personnel.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Supervision of accountable material destruction

controls.statement: Personnel supervising the destruction of media storing accountable material supervise its handling to the point of destruction, ensure that the destruction is completed successfully and sign a destruction certificate afterwards.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Supervision of accountable material destruction

controls.statement: The destruction of media storing accountable material is not outsourced.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Outsourcing media destruction

controls.statement: When outsourcing the destruction of media storing non-accountable material, a National Association for Information Destruction AAA certified destruction service with endorsements, as specified in ASIO’s Protective Security Circular-167, is used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media destruction / Outsourcing media destruction

controls.statement: Media disposal processes, and supporting media disposal procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media disposal / Media disposal processes and procedures

controls.statement: Labels and markings indicating the owner, sensitivity, classification or any other marking that can associate media with its prior use are removed prior to its disposal.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media disposal / Disposal of media

controls.statement: Following sanitisation, destruction or declassification, a formal administrative decision is made to release media, or its waste, into the public domain.
controls.topic: Guidelines for media / Media disposal / Disposal of media

controls.statement: Vendors that have demonstrated a commitment to Secure by Design and Secure by Default principles and practices, including secure programming practices and either memory-safe programming languages or less preferably memory-safe programming practices, are used for operating systems.
controls.topic: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Operating system selection

controls.statement: The latest release, or the previous release, of operating systems are used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Operating system releases and versions

controls.statement: Where supported, 64-bit versions of operating systems are used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Operating system releases and versions

controls.statement: SOEs are used for workstations and servers.
controls.topic: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Standard Operating Environments

controls.statement: SOEs provided by third parties are scanned for malicious code and configurations.
controls.topic: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Standard Operating Environments

controls.statement: SOEs are reviewed and updated at least annually.
controls.topic: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Standard Operating Environments

controls.statement: Approved configurations for operating systems are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations

controls.statement: Operating systems are hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur.
controls.topic: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations

controls.statement: Microsoft’s attack surface reduction rules are implemented.
controls.topic: Guidelines for system hardening / Operating system hardening / Hardening operating system configurations

controls.statement: Default user accounts or credentials for operating systems, including for any pre-configured user accounts, are changed, disabled or removed during initial setup.

controls.statement:
Services are configured with a session lock that:

- activates after a maximum of 15 minutes of user inactivity, a maximum of 12 hours of overall session time or when manually activated by users
- blocks access to all session content
- requires users to re-authenticate using all authentication factors to unlock the session
- denies users the ability to disable the session locking mechanism.
controls.topic: Guidelines for system hardening / Authentication hardening / Session locking

controls.statement:
Systems are configured with a screen lock that:

- activates after a maximum of 15 minutes of user inactivity, or when manually activated by users
- conceals all content on the screen
- ensures that the screen does not enter a power saving state before the screen lock is activated
- requires users to re-authenticate using all authentication factors to unlock the system
- denies users the ability to disable the screen locking mechanism.

controls.statement: Secure by Default principles and practices are followed throughout the software development life cycle, including by ensuring that all built-in security measures are included and enabled in the base product at no extra cost to consumers.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: SecDevOps practices are used for software development.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Software is architected and structured to support readability and maintainability.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Files containing executable content are digitally signed by a certificate with a verifiable chain of trust as part of software development.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Installers, patches and updates are digitally signed or provided with cryptographic checksums as part of software development.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Software has no default credentials; however, if credentials are required, they are created on first install by the installing organisation.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Application backwards compatibility does not compromise any security measures or features.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Where software allows user impersonation, sensitive data is not logged and appropriate permissions are set.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Where software allows an authentication factor to be reset, the user is notified of the reset through a secondary channel.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Where software supports multiple user roles, non-administrative users are prevented from altering their profile permissions or privileges.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: When user permissions or credentials are changed, software forces all impacted users to re-authenticate.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: When digital signatures are processed by software, they are validated against a certificate trust chain and checked for revocation using a Certificate Revocation List or with the Online Certificate Status Protocol.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Software generates sufficient event logs to support the detection of cyber security events.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Event logs produced by software ensure that any sensitive data is protected.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: Secure configuration guidance, in the form of a hardening guide or loosening guide, is produced and made available to consumers as part of software development.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: End of life procedures for software, including procedures for software removal and the archival or destruction of user accounts and data, are produced and made available to consumers.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Secure software development

controls.statement: If a software bill of materials is available for imported third-party software components, it is used during software development to ensure such software components have no known vulnerabilities.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software bill of materials

controls.statement: A software bill of materials is produced and made available to consumers of software.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software bill of materials

controls.statement: If a cryptographic bill of materials is available for imported third-party software components, it is used during software development to ensure such software components provide support for standardised implementations of ASD-Approved Cryptographic Algorithms.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Cryptographic bill of materials

controls.statement: A cryptographic bill of materials is produced and made available to consumers of software.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Cryptographic bill of materials

controls.statement: If a software build provenance is available for imported third-party software components, it is used during software development to ensure such software components are built to an appropriate standard.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software build provenance

controls.statement: A software build provenance is produced and made available to consumers of software.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software build provenance

controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Network application programming interfaces

controls.statement: Authentication and authorisation of clients is performed when clients call network APIs that facilitate modification of data but are not accessible over the internet.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Network application programming interfaces

controls.statement: Authentication and authorisation of clients is performed when clients call network APIs that facilitate access to data not authorised for release into the public domain and are accessible over the internet.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Network application programming interfaces

controls.statement: Authentication and authorisation of clients is performed when clients call network APIs that facilitate access to data not authorised for release into the public domain but are not accessible over the internet.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Network application programming interfaces

controls.statement: Network API calls that facilitate modification of data, or access to data not authorised for release into the public domain, and are accessible over the internet, are centrally logged.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Network application programming interfaces

controls.statement: Network API calls that facilitate modification of data, or access to data not authorised for release into the public domain, but are not accessible over the internet, are centrally logged.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Network application programming interfaces

controls.statement: Validation and sanitisation are performed on all input received over the internet by software.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software input handling

controls.statement: Validation and sanitisation are performed on all input received over a local network by software.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software input handling

controls.statement: All input validation rules are documented, implemented in code, and tested using both positive and negative unit tests and integration tests.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software input handling

controls.statement: Data sources and serialised data inputs are validated before being deserialised.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software input handling

controls.statement: File uploads or input are restricted to specific file types, with malicious content scanning occurring prior to file access, file execution or file storage.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software input handling

controls.statement: All queries to databases from software are filtered for legitimate content and correct syntax.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software interaction with databases

controls.statement: Parameterised queries or stored procedures, instead of dynamically generated queries, are used by software for database interactions.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software interaction with databases

controls.statement: Software is designed or configured to provide as little error information as possible about the structure of databases.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software interaction with databases

controls.statement: All queries to databases from software that are initiated by users, and any resulting crash or error messages, are centrally logged.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software interaction with databases

controls.statement: Peer reviews are conducted on all critical and security-related software components.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software security testing

controls.statement: Code reviews are utilised to ensure software components meets Secure by Design principles and practices as well as secure programming practices.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software security testing

controls.statement: Unit testing and integration testing, covering both positive and negative use cases, are used for software components to ensure code quality and correctness.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software security testing

controls.statement: Software is comprehensively tested for vulnerabilities using SAST, DAST and SCA prior to its initial release, any subsequent release, and periodically to help identify any previously unidentified vulnerabilities.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software security testing

controls.statement: Suitable AI models are used to augment software security testing.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software security testing

controls.statement: A vulnerability disclosure program is implemented to assist with the secure development and maintenance of products and services.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Vulnerability disclosure program

controls.statement: A vulnerability disclosure policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Vulnerability disclosure program

controls.statement: Vulnerability disclosure processes, and supporting vulnerability disclosure procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Vulnerability disclosure program

controls.statement: A ‘security.txt’ file is hosted for each of an organisation’s internet-facing website domains to assist in the responsible disclosure of vulnerabilities in the organisation’s products and services.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Vulnerability disclosure program

controls.statement: Vulnerabilities identified in software are publicly disclosed in a responsible and timely manner, including with Common Weakness Enumeration and Common Platform Enumeration information.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Reporting and resolving vulnerabilities

controls.statement: Vulnerabilities identified in software are resolved in a timely manner.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Reporting and resolving vulnerabilities

controls.statement: In resolving vulnerabilities, root cause analysis is performed and, to the greatest extent possible, entire vulnerability classes are remediated.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Reporting and resolving vulnerabilities

controls.statement: Security-relevant usage, error messages and crashes for software are centrally logged.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Software development fundamentals / Software event logging

controls.statement: AI-specific documentation, including AI model cards and AI system cards (or equivalent artefacts), is used to document AI model characteristics, system architectures, use cases and security risks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Secure artificial intelligence application development

controls.statement: AI models are stored in a non-executable file format that does not allow arbitrary code execution.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Secure artificial intelligence application development

controls.statement: The exposure of exact AI model confidence scores in API outputs or user interfaces is prevented.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Secure artificial intelligence application development

controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Data collection, retention and use

controls.statement: All prompts and outputs associated with chat sessions are securely deleted when chat sessions are removed from AI applications.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Data collection, retention and use

controls.statement: The source and integrity of AI models, structures and weights are verified.

controls.statement: The source and integrity of training data for AI models is verified.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Artificial intelligence model poisoning

controls.statement: Data validation and verification techniques are used to ensure the reliability and accuracy of training data used by AI models.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Artificial intelligence model poisoning

controls.statement: AI model performance metrics are monitored and anomalies are investigated.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Unbounded consumption

controls.statement: Rate limiting is applied to inference queries for AI models.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Unbounded consumption

controls.statement: Resource limits are enforced for AI models.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Unbounded consumption

controls.statement: Access control policies are implemented to enforce fine-grained permissions for AI applications.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Excessive agency

controls.statement: Role-based access controls are implemented for AI applications to restrict access to sensitive data.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Excessive agency

controls.statement: Generative AI applications evaluate user prompts to detect and mitigate adversarial inputs or suffixes designed to elicit unintended behaviour or assist in the generation of sensitive or harmful content.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Prompt injection

controls.statement: Content filtering is implemented by AI applications to detect and block sensitive data exposure and improper output.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Artificial intelligence application development / Sensitive data exposure and improper output

controls.statement: The OWASP Mobile Application Security Verification Standard is used in the development of mobile applications.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Mobile application development / Secure mobile application development

controls.statement: Robust web application frameworks are used in the development of web applications.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development

controls.statement: The OWASP Application Security Verification Standard is used in the development of web applications.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development

controls.statement: The OWASP Top 10 Proactive Controls are used in the development of web applications.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development

controls.statement: The OWASP Top 10 are mitigated in the development of web applications.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development

controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development

controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development

controls.statement: Web applications that support Single Sign On equally support Single Logout.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Secure web application design and development

controls.statement: Content-Security-Policy, Hypertext Transfer Protocol Strict Transport Security and X-Frame-Options are specified by web server software via security policy in response headers.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Web security policy response headers

controls.statement: All web application content is offered exclusively using HTTPS.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Web application interactions

controls.statement: The OWASP API Security Top 10 are mitigated in the development of web APIs.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Web application programming interfaces

controls.statement: Output encoding is performed on all output produced by web applications.
controls.topic: Guidelines for software development / Web application development / Web application output encoding

controls.statement: Database servers and web servers are functionally separated.
controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Functional separation between database servers and web servers

controls.statement: Data communicated between database servers and web servers is encrypted using Australian Signals Directorate-approved cryptography.
controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Communications between database servers and web servers

controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Network environment

controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Network environment

controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Network environment

controls.statement: Database servers for development, testing, staging and production environments are segregated.
controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Database servers / Segregation of development, testing, staging and production database servers

controls.statement: A database register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.
controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Database register

controls.statement: File-based access controls are applied to database files.
controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Protecting databases

controls.statement: Databases and their contents are classified based on the sensitivity or classification of data that they contain.
controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Protecting database contents

controls.statement: Database users’ ability to access, insert, modify and remove database contents is restricted based on their work duties.
controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Protecting database contents

controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Segregation of development, testing, staging and production databases

controls.statement:
Security-relevant events for databases are centrally logged, including:

- access or modification of particularly important content
- addition of new users, especially privileged users
- changes to user roles or privileges
- attempts to elevate user privileges
- queries containing comments
- queries containing multiple embedded queries
- database and query alerts or failures
- database structure changes
- database administrator actions
- use of executable commands
- database logons and logoffs.
controls.topic: Guidelines for database systems / Databases / Database event logging

controls.statement: An email usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Email usage policy

controls.statement: Access to non-approved webmail services is blocked.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Webmail services

controls.statement: Protective markings are applied to emails and reflect the highest sensitivity or classification of the subject, body and attachments.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Protective markings for emails

controls.statement: Protective marking tools do not automatically insert protective markings into emails.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Protective marking tools

controls.statement: Protective marking tools do not allow users to select protective markings that a system has not been authorised to process, store or communicate.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Protective marking tools

controls.statement: Protective marking tools do not allow users replying to or forwarding emails to select protective markings lower than previously used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Protective marking tools

controls.statement: Email servers are configured to block, log and report emails with inappropriate protective markings.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Handling emails with inappropriate, invalid or missing protective markings

controls.statement: The intended recipients of blocked inbound emails, and the senders of blocked outbound emails, are notified.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Handling emails with inappropriate, invalid or missing protective markings

controls.statement: Emails containing Australian Eyes Only, Australian Government Access Only or Releasable To data are not sent to email distribution lists unless the nationality of all members of email distribution lists can be confirmed.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email usage / Email distribution lists

controls.statement: Emails are routed via centralised email gateways.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Centralised email gateways

controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Centralised email gateways

controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Email gateway maintenance activities

controls.statement: Email servers only relay emails destined for or originating from their domains (including subdomains).
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Open relay email servers

controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Email server transport encryption

controls.statement: MTA-STS is enabled to prevent the unencrypted transfer of emails between email servers.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Email server transport encryption

controls.statement: SPF is used to specify authorised email servers (or lack thereof) for an organisation’s domains (including subdomains).
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Sender Policy Framework

controls.statement: A hard fail SPF record is used when specifying authorised email servers (or lack thereof) for an organisation’s domains (including subdomains).
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Sender Policy Framework

controls.statement: SPF is used to verify the authenticity of incoming emails.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Sender Policy Framework

controls.statement: DKIM signing is enabled on emails originating from an organisation’s domains (including subdomains).
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / DomainKeys Identified Mail

controls.statement: DKIM signatures on incoming emails are verified.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / DomainKeys Identified Mail

controls.statement: Email distribution list applications used by external senders is configured such that it does not break the validity of the sender’s DKIM signature.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / DomainKeys Identified Mail

controls.statement: Incoming emails are rejected if they do not pass DMARC checks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance

controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Email content filtering

controls.statement: Notifications of undeliverable emails are only sent to senders that can be verified via SPF or other trusted means.
controls.topic: Guidelines for email / Email gateways and servers / Notifications of undeliverable emails

controls.statement: Network documentation includes device settings for all critical servers, high-value servers, network devices and network security appliances.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network documentation

controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network documentation

controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network segmentation and segregation

controls.statement: Networked management interfaces for IT equipment are not directly exposed to the internet.

controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Functional separation between servers

controls.statement: Servers minimise communications with other servers at the network and file system level.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Functional separation between servers

controls.statement: All data communicated over network infrastructure is encrypted using ASD-approved cryptography.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network encryption

controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using Internet Protocol version 6

controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Using Internet Protocol version 6

controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network access controls

controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network management traffic

controls.statement: Outbound network connections to anonymity networks are blocked.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Blocking anonymity network traffic

controls.statement: Security-relevant events for non-internet-facing network devices are centrally logged.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Network design and configuration / Network device event logging
