controls.statement: The use of FT (802.11r) is disabled unless authenticator-to-authenticator communications are secured by an ASD-Approved Cryptographic Protocol.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Fast Basic Service Set Transition

controls.statement: Communications between authenticators and a RADIUS server are encapsulated with an additional layer of encryption using RADIUS over Internet Protocol Security or RADIUS over Transport Layer Security.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service authentication

controls.statement: Wireless networks implement sufficient frequency separation from other wireless networks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Interference between wireless networks

controls.statement: Wireless access points enable the use of the 802.11w amendment to protect management frames.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Protecting management frames on wireless networks

controls.statement: Instead of deploying a small number of wireless access points that broadcast on high power, a greater number of wireless access points that use less broadcast power are deployed to achieve the desired footprint for wireless networks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Wireless network footprint

controls.statement: The effective range of wireless communications outside an organisation’s area of control is limited by implementing RF shielding on facilities in which SECRET or TOP SECRET wireless networks are used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Wireless networks / Wireless network footprint

controls.statement: Cloud service providers are used for hosting online services.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Cloud-based hosting of online services

controls.statement: Cloud service providers’ ability to scale resources dynamically in response to genuine spikes in demand is discussed and verified as part of capacity and availability planning for online services.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Capacity and availability planning and monitoring for online services

controls.statement: Where a high availability requirement exists for online services, the services are architected to automatically transition between availability zones.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Capacity and availability planning and monitoring for online services

controls.statement: Continuous real-time monitoring of the capacity and availability of online services is performed.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Capacity and availability planning and monitoring for online services

controls.statement: Where a high availability requirement exists for website hosting, CDNs that cache websites are used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Using content delivery networks

controls.statement: If using CDNs, disclosing the IP addresses of web servers under an organisation’s control (referred to as origin servers) is avoided and access to the origin servers is restricted to the CDNs and authorised management networks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Using content delivery networks

controls.statement:
Denial-of-service attack mitigation strategies are discussed with cloud service providers, specifically:

- their capacity to withstand denial-of-service attacks
- costs likely to be incurred as a result of denial-of-service attacks
- availability monitoring and thresholds for notification of denial-of-service attacks
- thresholds for turning off any online services or functionality during denial-of-service attacks
- pre-approved actions that can be undertaken during denial-of-service attacks
- any arrangements with upstream service providers to block malicious network traffic as far upstream as possible.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Denial-of-service attack mitigation strategies

controls.statement: Critical online services are segregated from other online services that are more likely to be targeted as part of denial-of-service attacks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Denial-of-service attack mitigation strategies

controls.statement: Domain names for online services are protected via registrar locking and confirming that domain registration details are correct.
controls.topic: Guidelines for networking / Service continuity for online services / Denial-of-service attack mitigation strategies

controls.statement: Communications security doctrine and policy produced by ASD for the management and operation of HACE is complied with.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Communications security doctrine

controls.statement: HACE are issued an Approval for Use by ASD and operated in accordance with the latest version of their associated Australian Communications Security Instructions.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / High Assurance Cryptographic Equipment

controls.statement: Cryptographic key management processes, and supporting cryptographic key management procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Cryptographic key management processes and procedures

controls.statement: Cryptographic equipment, applications or libraries that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against an ASD-endorsed Protection Profile are used when encrypting media that contains OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED data.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Cryptographic implementation assurance

controls.statement: HACE is used when encrypting media that contains SECRET or TOP SECRET data.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Cryptographic implementation assurance

controls.statement: Cryptographic equipment, applications or libraries that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against an ASD-endorsed Protection Profile are used to protect OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED data when communicated over insufficiently secure networks, outside of appropriately secure areas or via public network infrastructure.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Cryptographic implementation assurance

controls.statement: HACE is used to protect SECRET and TOP SECRET data when communicated over insufficiently secure networks, outside of appropriately secure areas or via public network infrastructure.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Cryptographic implementation assurance

controls.statement: Where practical, cryptographic equipment, applications and libraries provide a means of data recovery to allow for circumstances where the encryption key is unavailable due to loss, damage or failure.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Data recovery

controls.statement: When a user authenticates to the encryption functionality of IT equipment or media, it is treated in accordance with its original sensitivity or classification until the user deauthenticates from the encryption functionality.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Handling encrypted IT equipment and media

controls.statement: Keyed cryptographic equipment is transported based on the sensitivity or classification of its keying material.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Transporting cryptographic equipment

controls.statement: The compromise or suspected compromise of cryptographic equipment or associated keying material is reported to the chief information security officer, or one of their delegates, as soon as possible after it occurs.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Reporting cryptographic-related cyber security incidents

controls.statement: Keying material is changed when compromised or suspected of being compromised.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic fundamentals / Reporting cryptographic-related cyber security incidents

controls.statement: An AACA or high assurance cryptographic algorithm is used when encrypting data at rest.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using cryptographic algorithms

controls.statement: Only AACAs or high assurance cryptographic algorithms are used by cryptographic equipment, applications and libraries.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using cryptographic algorithms

controls.statement: ECDH is used in preference to DH.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Asymmetric cryptographic algorithms

controls.statement: When using DH for agreeing on encryption session keys, a modulus of at least 2048 bits is used, preferably 3072 bits.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Diffie-Hellman

controls.statement: When using DH for agreeing on encryption session keys, a modulus of at least 3072 bits is used, preferably 3072 bits.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Diffie-Hellman

controls.statement: When using DH for agreeing on encryption session keys, a modulus and associated parameters are selected according to NIST SP 800-56A Rev. 3.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Diffie-Hellman

controls.statement: When using elliptic curve cryptography, a suitable curve from NIST SP 800-186 is used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Elliptic Curve Cryptography

controls.statement: When using ECDH for agreeing on encryption session keys, a base point order and key size of at least 224 bits is used, preferably the NIST P-384 curve.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman

controls.statement: When using ECDH for agreeing on encryption session keys, NIST P-256, P-384 or P-521 curves are used, preferably the NIST P-384 curve.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman

controls.statement: When using ECDH for agreeing on encryption session keys, NIST P-384 or P-521 curves are used, preferably the NIST P-384 curve.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman

controls.statement: When using ECDSA for digital signatures, a base point order and key size of at least 224 bits is used, preferably the P-384 curve.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm

controls.statement: When using ECDSA for digital signatures, NIST P-256, P-384 or P-521 curves are used, preferably the NIST P-384 curve.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm

controls.statement: When using ECDSA for digital signatures, NIST P-384 or P-521 curves are used, preferably the NIST P-384 curve.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm

controls.statement: When using ML-DSA and ML-KEM, as per FIPS 204 and FIPS 203 respectively, adherence to pre-requisite FIPS 140-3 validation is preferred.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using post-quantum cryptographic algorithms

controls.statement: When using ML-DSA for digital signatures, ML-DSA-65 or ML-DSA-87 is used, preferably ML-DSA-87.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm

controls.statement: When using ML-DSA for digital signatures, the hedged variant is used whenever possible.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm

controls.statement: Pre-hashed variants of ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 are only used when the performance of default variants is unacceptable.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm

controls.statement: When the pre-hashed variants of ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 are used, at least SHA-384 and SHA-512 respectively are used for pre-hashing.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm

controls.statement: When using ML-KEM for encapsulating encryption session keys (and similar keys), ML-KEM-768 or ML-KEM-1024 is used, preferably ML-KEM-1024.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using the Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism

controls.statement: When using RSA for digital signatures, and transporting encryption session keys (and similar keys), a modulus of at least 2048 bits is used, preferably 3072 bits.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Rivest-Shamir-Adleman

controls.statement: When using RSA for digital signatures, and transporting encryption session keys (and similar keys), a modulus of at least 3072 bits is used, preferably 3072 bits.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Rivest-Shamir-Adleman

controls.statement: When using RSA for digital signatures, and for transporting encryption session keys (and similar keys), a different key pair is used for digital signatures and transporting encryption session keys.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Rivest-Shamir-Adleman

controls.statement: When using SHA-2 for hashing, an output size of at least 224 bits is used, preferably SHA-384 or SHA-512.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Secure Hashing Algorithms

controls.statement: When using SHA-2 for hashing, an output size of at least 256 bits is used, preferably SHA-384 or SHA-512.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Secure Hashing Algorithms

controls.statement: When using SHA-2 for hashing, an output size of at least 384 bits is used, preferably SHA-384 or SHA-512.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using Secure Hashing Algorithms

controls.statement: When using AES for encryption, AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256 is used, preferably AES-256.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using symmetric cryptographic algorithms

controls.statement: When using AES for encryption, AES-192 or AES-256 is used, preferably AES-256.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using symmetric cryptographic algorithms

controls.statement: Symmetric cryptographic algorithms are not used in Electronic Codebook Mode.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Using symmetric cryptographic algorithms

controls.statement: A post-quantum cryptography transition plan is developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Transitioning to post-quantum cryptography

controls.statement: The development and procurement of new cryptographic equipment, applications and libraries ensures support for the use of ML-DSA-87, ML-KEM-1024, SHA-384, SHA-512 and AES-256 by no later than 2030.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Transitioning to post-quantum cryptography

controls.statement: When a post-quantum traditional hybrid scheme is used, either the post-quantum cryptographic algorithm, the traditional cryptographic algorithm or both are AACAs.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic algorithms / Post-quantum traditional hybrid schemes

controls.statement: An AACP or high assurance cryptographic protocol is used when encrypting data in transit.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic protocols / Using cryptographic protocols

controls.statement: Only AACPs or high assurance cryptographic protocols are used by cryptographic equipment, applications and libraries.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Cryptographic protocols / Using cryptographic protocols

controls.statement: Only the latest version of TLS is used for TLS connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security

controls.statement: AES-GCM is used for encryption of TLS connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security

controls.statement: Only server-initiated secure renegotiation is used for TLS connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security

controls.statement: DH or ECDH is used for key establishment of TLS connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security

controls.statement: When using DH or ECDH for key establishment of TLS connections, the ephemeral variant is used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security

controls.statement: Anonymous DH is not used for TLS connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security

controls.statement: SHA-2-based certificates are used for TLS connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security

controls.statement: SHA-2 is used for the Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) and pseudorandom function (PRF) for TLS connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security

controls.statement: TLS compression is disabled for TLS connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security

controls.statement: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) is used for TLS connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Transport Layer Security / Configuring Transport Layer Security

controls.statement: The use of SSH version 1 is disabled for SSH connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Configuring Secure Shell

controls.statement:
The SSH daemon is configured to:

- only listen on the required interfaces (ListenAddress xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx)
- have a suitable login banner (Banner x)
- have a login authentication timeout of no more than 60 seconds (LoginGraceTime 60)
- disable host-based authentication (HostbasedAuthentication no)
- disable rhosts-based authentication (IgnoreRhosts yes)
- disable the ability to log in directly as root (PermitRootLogin no)
- disable empty passwords (PermitEmptyPasswords no)
- disable connection forwarding (AllowTCPForwarding no)
- disable gateway ports (GatewayPorts no)
- disable X11 forwarding (X11Forwarding no).
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Configuring Secure Shell

controls.statement: Public key-based authentication is used for SSH connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Authentication mechanisms

controls.statement: SSH private keys are protected with a password or a key encryption key.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Authentication mechanisms

controls.statement:
When using logins without a password for SSH connections, the following are disabled:

- access from IP addresses that do not require access
- port forwarding
- agent credential forwarding
- X11 forwarding
- console access.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Automated remote access

controls.statement: If using remote access without the use of a password for SSH connections, the ‘forced command’ option is used to specify what command is executed and parameter checking is enabled.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / Automated remote access

controls.statement: When SSH-agent or similar key caching applications are used, it is limited to workstations and servers with screen locks and key caches that are set to expire within four hours of inactivity.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure Shell / SSH-agent

controls.statement: Versions of S/MIME earlier than S/MIME version 3.0 are not used for S/MIME connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extension / Configuring Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extension

controls.statement: Tunnel mode is used for IPsec connections; however, if using transport mode, an IP tunnel is used.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Mode of operation

controls.statement: The ESP protocol is used for authentication and encryption of IPsec connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Protocol selection

controls.statement: IKE version 2 is used for key exchange when establishing IPsec connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Key exchange

controls.statement: AES is used for encrypting IPsec connections, preferably ENCR_AES_GCM_16.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Encryption algorithms

controls.statement: PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256, PRF_HMAC_SHA2_384 or PRF_HMAC_SHA2_512 is used for IPsec connections, preferably PRF_HMAC_SHA2_512.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Pseudorandom function

controls.statement: AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128, AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_384_192, AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_512_256 or NONE (only with AES-GCM) is used for authenticating IPsec connections, preferably NONE.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Integrity algorithms

controls.statement: DH or ECDH is used for key establishment of IPsec connections, preferably 384-bit random ECP group, 3072-bit MODP Group or 4096-bit MODP Group.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Diffie-Hellman groups

controls.statement: A security association lifetime of less than four hours (14400 seconds) is used for IPsec connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Security association lifetimes

controls.statement: PFS is used for IPsec connections.
controls.topic: Guidelines for cryptography / Internet Protocol Security / Perfect Forward Secrecy

controls.statement: Gateways are implemented between networks belonging to different security domains.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Implementing gateways

controls.statement: Gateways implement a demilitarised zone if external parties require access to an organisation’s services.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Implementing gateways

controls.statement: Gateways only allow explicitly authorised data flows.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Implementing gateways

controls.statement: Gateways inspect and filter data flows at the transport and above network layers.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Implementing gateways

controls.statement: Gateways perform ingress traffic filtering to detect and prevent IP source address spoofing.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Implementing gateways

controls.statement: System administrators for gateways undergo appropriate employment screening, and where necessary hold an appropriate security clearance, based on the sensitivity or classification of gateways.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways

controls.statement: System administrators for gateways that connect to Australian Eyes Only or Releasable To networks are Australian nationals.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways

controls.statement: System administrators for gateways that connect to Australian Government Access Only networks are Australian nationals or seconded foreign nationals.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways

controls.statement: System administrators for gateways are assigned the minimum privileges required to perform their duties.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways

controls.statement: Separation of duties is implemented in performing administrative activities for gateways.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways

controls.statement: System administrators for gateways are formally trained on the operation and management of gateways.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administrators for gateways

controls.statement: Gateways are managed via a secure path isolated from all connected networks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administration of gateways

controls.statement: For gateways between networks belonging to different security domains, any shared components are managed by system administrators for the higher security domain or by system administrators from a mutually agreed upon third party.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / System administration of gateways

controls.statement: Users authenticate to other networks accessed via gateways.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Authenticating to networks accessed via gateways

controls.statement: IT equipment authenticates to other networks accessed via gateways.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Authenticating to networks accessed via gateways

controls.statement: Public IP addresses controlled by, or used by, an organisation are signed by valid ROA records.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Border Gateway Protocol routing security

controls.statement: Routes for RPKI-registered IP addresses that are advertised from invalid Autonomous Systems, or that are longer than allowed, are rejected or deprioritised by routers that exchange routes via BGP.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Border Gateway Protocol routing security

controls.statement:
Security-relevant events for gateways are centrally logged, including:

- data packets and data flows permitted through gateways
- data packets and data flows attempting to leave gateways
- real-time alerts for attempted intrusions.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Gateway event logging

controls.statement: Gateways undergo testing following configuration changes, and at regular intervals no more than six months apart, to validate that they conform to expected security configurations.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Assessment of gateways

controls.statement: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive, PROTECTED and SECRET gateways undergo an IRAP assessment, using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the IRAP assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Assessment of gateways

controls.statement: TOP SECRET gateways undergo a security assessment by ASD assessors (or their delegates), using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Gateways / Assessment of gateways

controls.statement: CDSs are implemented between SECRET or TOP SECRET networks and any other networks belonging to different security domains.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Cross Domain Solutions / Implementing Cross Domain Solutions

controls.statement: When planning, designing, implementing or introducing additional connectivity to CDSs, ASD is consulted and any directions provided by ASD are complied with.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Cross Domain Solutions / Consultation on Cross Domain Solutions

controls.statement: CDSs implement isolated upward and downward network paths.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Cross Domain Solutions / Separation of data flows

controls.statement: CDSs implement independent security-enforcing functions for upward and downward network paths.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Cross Domain Solutions / Separation of data flows

controls.statement: CDSs implement protocol breaks at each network layer.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Cross Domain Solutions / Separation of data flows

controls.statement: Security-relevant events for CDSs are centrally logged.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Cross Domain Solutions / Cross Domain Solution event logging

controls.statement: A sample of security-relevant events relating to data transfer policies are taken at least every three months and assessed against security policies for CDSs to identify any operational failures.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Cross Domain Solutions / Cross Domain Solution event logging

controls.statement: Users are trained on the secure use of CDSs before access is granted.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Cross Domain Solutions / User training

controls.statement: Evaluated firewalls are used between an organisation’s networks and public network infrastructure.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Firewalls / Using firewalls

controls.statement: Evaluated firewalls are used between networks belonging to different security domains.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Firewalls / Using firewalls

controls.statement: If using a WAF, disclosing the IP addresses of web servers under an organisation’s control (referred to as origin servers) is avoided and access to the origin servers is restricted to the WAF and authorised management networks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Web application firewalls / Using web application firewalls

controls.statement: Evaluated diodes are used for controlling the data flow of unidirectional gateways between an organisation’s networks and public network infrastructure.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Diodes / Using diodes

controls.statement: Evaluated diodes used for controlling the data flow of unidirectional gateways between SECRET or TOP SECRET networks and public network infrastructure complete a high assurance evaluation.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Diodes / Using diodes

controls.statement: Evaluated diodes are used for controlling the data flow of unidirectional gateways between networks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Diodes / Using diodes

controls.statement: Evaluated diodes used for controlling the data flow of unidirectional gateways between SECRET or TOP SECRET networks and any other networks complete a high assurance evaluation.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Diodes / Using diodes

controls.statement: All web access, including that by internal servers, is conducted through web proxies.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Web proxies / Using web proxies

controls.statement:
The following details are centrally logged for websites accessed via web proxies:

- web address
- date and time
- user
- amount of data uploaded and downloaded
- internal and external IP addresses.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Web proxies / Web proxy event logging

controls.statement: Web content filtering is implemented to filter potentially harmful web-based content.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Using web content filters

controls.statement: Client-side active content is restricted by web content filters to an organisation-approved list of domain names.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Using web content filters

controls.statement: Web content filtering is applied to outbound web traffic where appropriate.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Using web content filters

controls.statement: TLS traffic communicated through gateways is decrypted and inspected.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Transport Layer Security filtering

controls.statement: An organisation-approved list of domain names, or list of website categories, is implemented for all Hypertext Transfer Protocol and Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure traffic communicated through gateways.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Allowing and blocking access to domain names

controls.statement: Malicious domain names, dynamic domain names and domain names that can be registered anonymously for free are blocked by web content filters.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Allowing and blocking access to domain names

controls.statement: Attempts to access websites through their IP addresses instead of their domain names are blocked by web content filters.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Web content filters / Allowing and blocking access to domain names

controls.statement: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo content filtering checks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Performing content filtering

controls.statement: Files identified by content filtering checks as malicious, or that cannot be inspected, are blocked.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Performing content filtering

controls.statement: Files identified by content filtering checks as suspicious are quarantined until reviewed and subsequently approved or not approved for release.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Performing content filtering

controls.statement: Content filters used by CDSs undergo rigorous security testing to ensure they perform as expected and cannot be bypassed.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Performing content filtering

controls.statement: Encrypted files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs are decrypted to undergo content filtering checks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Encrypted files

controls.statement: Archive files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs are unpacked to undergo content filtering checks.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Archive files

controls.statement: Archive files are unpacked in a controlled manner to ensure content filter performance or availability is not adversely affected.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Archive files

controls.statement: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo antivirus scanning using multiple different scanning engines.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Antivirus scanning

controls.statement: Executable files imported via gateways or CDSs are automatically executed in a sandbox to detect any suspicious behaviour.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Automated dynamic analysis

controls.statement: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs are filtered for allowed file types.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Allowing specific content types

controls.statement: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo content validation.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Content validation

controls.statement: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo content checking.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Content checking

controls.statement: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo content conversion.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Content conversion

controls.statement: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo content sanitisation.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Content sanitisation

controls.statement: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs that have a digital signature or cryptographic checksum are validated.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Content filtering / Validating file integrity

controls.statement: Evaluated peripheral switches are used when sharing peripherals between systems.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Peripheral switches / Using peripheral switches

controls.statement: Evaluated peripheral switches used for sharing peripherals between SECRET and TOP SECRET systems, or between SECRET or TOP SECRET systems belonging to different security domains, preferably complete a high assurance evaluation.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Peripheral switches / Using peripheral switches

controls.statement: Evaluated peripheral switches used for sharing peripherals between SECRET or TOP SECRET systems and any non-SECRET or TOP SECRET systems complete a high assurance evaluation.
controls.topic: Guidelines for gateways / Peripheral switches / Using peripheral switches

controls.statement: Data transfer processes, and supporting data transfer procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Data transfer processes and procedures

controls.statement: Processes, and supporting procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained to prevent AUSTEO, AGAO and REL data in textual and non-textual formats from being exported to unsuitable foreign systems.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Data transfer processes and procedures

controls.statement: Users transferring data to and from systems are held accountable for data transfers they perform.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / User responsibilities

controls.statement: When manually importing data to systems, the data is scanned for malicious and active content.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Manual import of data

controls.statement: When manually importing data to systems, all data that fails security checks is quarantined until reviewed and subsequently approved or not approved for release.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Manual import of data

controls.statement: Data exported from SECRET and TOP SECRET systems is reviewed and authorised by a trustworthy source beforehand.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Authorising export of data

controls.statement: Data authorised for export from SECRET and TOP SECRET systems is digitally signed by a trustworthy source.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Authorising export of data

controls.statement: Trustworthy sources for SECRET and TOP SECRET systems are limited to people and services that have been verified and authorised as such by the chief information security officer.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Authorising export of data

controls.statement: When manually exporting data from systems, the data is checked for unsuitable protective markings.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Manual export of data

controls.statement: When manually exporting data from SECRET and TOP SECRET systems, digital signatures are validated and keyword checks are performed within all textual data.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Manual export of data

controls.statement: When manually exporting data from systems, all data that fails security checks is quarantined until reviewed and subsequently approved or not approved for release.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Manual export of data

controls.statement: Data transfer logs are used to record all data imports and exports from systems.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Monitoring data import and export

controls.statement: Data transfer logs for systems are partially verified at least monthly.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Monitoring data import and export

controls.statement: Data transfer logs for SECRET and TOP SECRET systems are fully verified at least monthly.
controls.topic: Guidelines for data transfers / Data transfers / Monitoring data import and export
